## Selecting Technology Corners {#sec-technology-corners}

An extraction corner selects the data used to calculate parasitics. It does not automatically select transistor models, temperature or supply voltage for the subsequent simulation. Those choices can be independent in an open PDK.

::: {.callout-note}
Corner selection belongs to the development version following `0.9.0`. Each supported technology supplies complete `nominal`, `low` and `high` capacitance components. A custom scenario can select those components explicitly.

The development catalogs also provide:

- Isolated IHP `GatPoly` sheet-resistance sensitivities (@sec-corner-gatpoly-sheet)
- Complete `ihp-sg13cmos5l` fixed-layout resistance sensitivities (@sec-corner-cmos5l-resistance)
- `sky130A` resistance sensitivities with explicit MIM sheet bounds (@sec-corner-sky130-resistance)
- `gf180mcuD` resistance sensitivities with explicit plate and ideal-contact assumptions (@sec-corner-gf180-resistance)
- Independent MIM device-reference components (@sec-corner-device-references)
- Source-related physical recipes (@sec-corner-physical-recipes)

These selections retain their documented assumptions. An upstream style name does not automatically declare a matching physical stack or a correlated process corner.
:::

### Selecting Declared Scenarios {#sec-corner-selection}

Both `kpex extract` and `kpex pex25d` accept `--corner`. A scenario names complete resistance, capacitance, physical-stack and optional device-reference datasets. With no explicit option, the catalog's declared default is selected.

```bash
kpex extract --pdk sky130A --2.5D --mode RC --corner nominal \
  --gds r_wire_voltage_divider_li1.gds.gz \
  --out-netlist divider.spice --out-result divider-result.json
```

GDS: <https://github.com/iic-jku/klayout-pex/blob/main/testdata/designs/sky130A/test_patterns/r_wire_voltage_divider_li1.gds.gz>

This example uses the bundled nominal data and a distributed wire pattern. Omitting `--corner nominal` produces the same technology selection while `nominal` is the catalog default.

A separately supplied catalog can be selected explicitly:

```bash
kpex extract --pdk sky130A --2.5D --mode RC \
  --tech-catalog path/to/catalog.pb.json --corner nominal \
  --gds r_wire_voltage_divider_li1.gds.gz \
  --out-netlist divider.spice
```

The catalog must identify the selected `--pdk`. A catalog for one process cannot silently change the layout/LVS interface of another. Scenario identifiers are case-sensitive: `nominal` and `Nominal` are different names.

Unknown selections fail before the layout or LVS database is read. The diagnostic lists the valid scenarios, so a typo cannot silently fall back to nominal extraction.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Keeping the Sources Independent {#sec-corner-components}

The four datasets answer different physical questions:

| Dataset | What it determines |
|:---|:---|
| Resistance | Sheet resistance and per-cut contact/via resistance |
| Capacitance | Area, sidewall and fringe coefficients, including fitted offsets and halo |
| Physical stack | Layer positions, film thicknesses and dielectric constants for geometry generation |
| Device references | Independent capacitance estimates used by device checks |
: Component datasets selected by a scenario {#tbl-corner-components tbl-colwidths="[26,74]"}

Layout layers, computed-layer identities, device interfaces, substrate connectivity and exclusion definitions remain shared. Selection resolves a fresh complete technology before extraction caches are constructed. Running one corner and then another does not accumulate table rows or modify a previous selection.

{{< include /figures/technology-corner-selection.qmd >}}

A missing table entry is not the same as an explicit zero. Each selected resistance and capacitance table must cover the same row keys as the default scenario. Complete components can be shared by several scenarios without inheriting unspecified numerical entries from nominal data.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Tracing Sources and Assumptions {#sec-corner-source-provenance}

Each catalog and dataset has structured `provenance`:

| Field | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| `data_revision` | Authored revision of this catalog or dataset |
| `sources` | Source identifiers, descriptions, URIs, revisions, hashes and preprocessing options |
| `assumptions` | Explicit projections or approximations, their reasons and supporting source identifiers |
| `history` | Dated changes with their revision, summary, reason, source identifiers and review links |
: Evidence accompanying technology data {#tbl-corner-provenance-fields tbl-colwidths="[28,72]"}

A source must identify a revision or an exact SHA256 digest. Extraction records these references without downloading them. A source revision identifies the input document, while `data_revision` identifies the KPEX interpretation of that input. The two can change independently.

For example, the `ihp-sg13g2` capacitance dataset identifies the corrected extraction file at `14b1ab8`. Its resistance dataset separately records the nominal `GatPoly` and MIM assumptions. The device-reference dataset cites its independent MOM models. A common process name does not make those sources interchangeable.

An assumption states both what was assumed and why. Diffusion projection and the thin-plate approximation for surrounding MIM coupling therefore remain visible alongside the imported coefficients. Recording an assumption does not establish a measured error bound or qualify a physical corner.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Maintaining Data History {#sec-corner-data-history}

Maintain history when reviewing a data change:

1. Add new source records for changed upstream inputs, with new identifiers and pinned revisions or hashes
2. Describe changed assumptions and their physical reasons
3. Append a history entry with the change date, summary, reason and supporting source or review references
4. Set `data_revision` to that final entry's revision, then regenerate the files and their catalog hashes
5. Compare the numerical tables and check the affected geometries and sibling variants

Keep previous history entries and the source identities they reference unchanged. Entries are ordered from oldest to newest. Multiple revisions on one date are allowed. A build does not invent a new revision or timestamp, and revision labels are not interpreted as corner names or version ranges.

The catalog's history describes its available components and declared scenarios. Each component retains its own history, so updating capacitance does not invent a resistance or physical-stack revision.

`schema_version` describes the catalog format. `data_revision` describes the data and its interpretation. File hashes identify exact serialized bytes, while the resolved payload hashes identify numerical inputs. A clarification of an assumption changes file identity without changing coefficient identity.

The technology format is under development before `1.0.0`. After a schema change, regenerate the examples with the matching KPEX version. Assigned field numbers and JSON names will become compatibility contracts when the format is stabilized.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Reading Upstream Corner Names {#sec-corner-upstream-names}

The maintained `MAGIC` extraction decks for the supported technologies declare these R/C combinations:

| Style suffix | Resistance | Capacitance |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Nominal style | Nominal | Nominal |
| `hrhc` | High | High |
| `hrlc` | High | Low |
| `lrhc` | Low | High |
| `lrlc` | Low | Low |
: Explicit upstream extraction combinations, distinct from bundled availability {#tbl-corner-upstream-styles tbl-colwidths="[40,30,30]"}

The sources are the maintained [OpenPDKs `sky130` deck](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/open-pdks/blob/5740c4a81c42f9fe4af5ef2ee258a99151053d28/sky130/magic/sky130-extract.tech), [OpenPDKs `gf180mcu` deck](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/open-pdks/blob/5740c4a81c42f9fe4af5ef2ee258a99151053d28/gf180mcu/magic/gf180mcu-extract.tech), and the corrected [`ihp-sg13g2`](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK/blob/14b1ab845696960a0a1881ec8614acba0f7b8eb7/ihp-sg13g2/libs.tech/magic/ihp-sg13g2-extract.tech) and [`ihp-sg13cmos5l`](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK/blob/14b1ab845696960a0a1881ec8614acba0f7b8eb7/ihp-sg13cmos5l/libs.tech/magic/ihp-sg13cmos5l-extract.tech) decks.

These names do not define all nine products of low, nominal and high R/C. Nor do transistor labels such as `tt`, `ff` and `ss` imply an extraction corner. For example, the [`sky130` simulation library](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/skywater-pdk-libs-sky130_fd_pr/blob/29b55153fd9f4badef05a02667184b81789d1f61/models/sky130.lib.spice) separates MOS corner selection from its R/C model sections.

KPEX also contains derived MIM and diffusion rows and resistance values from other process sources. An imported corner must resolve those rows explicitly. The presence of a high-C block in an extraction deck is not evidence for an otherwise undocumented MIM sheet-resistance limit.

Separate component files do not imply statistical independence of R and C. In `sky130A`, some resistance-model overrides differ between `hrhc` and `hrlc`, even though both names start with high R. Such sources require scenario-specific R datasets rather than one generic high-R component.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Using Low/High Capacitance Components {#sec-corner-low-high-capacitance}

Each supported PDK has complete `nominal`, `low` and `high` capacitance datasets. The additional components cover substrate area and perimeter, overlap, fitted sidewall and directed fringe terms. They retain the diffusion projections and MIM construction used by the nominal technology, with the selected capacitance data.

| Technology | Capacitance datasets | Selection examples |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `sky130A` | [`nominal`](../data/tech/sky130A/capacitance/nominal.pb.json), [`low`](../data/tech/sky130A/capacitance/low.pb.json), [`high`](../data/tech/sky130A/capacitance/high.pb.json) | `nominal`; R/C sensitivities in @sec-corner-sky130-resistance |
| `gf180mcuD` | [`nominal`](../data/tech/gf180mcuD/capacitance/nominal.pb.json), [`low`](../data/tech/gf180mcuD/capacitance/low.pb.json), [`high`](../data/tech/gf180mcuD/capacitance/high.pb.json) | `nominal`; R-only sensitivities in @sec-corner-gf180-resistance |
| `ihp-sg13g2` | [`nominal`](../data/tech/ihp-sg13g2/capacitance/nominal.pb.json), [`low`](../data/tech/ihp-sg13g2/capacitance/low.pb.json), [`high`](../data/tech/ihp-sg13g2/capacitance/high.pb.json) | `nominal`; `GatPoly` sensitivities in @sec-corner-gatpoly-sheet |
| `ihp-sg13cmos5l` | [`nominal`](../data/tech/ihp-sg13cmos5l/capacitance/nominal.pb.json), [`low`](../data/tech/ihp-sg13cmos5l/capacitance/low.pb.json), [`high`](../data/tech/ihp-sg13cmos5l/capacitance/high.pb.json) | `nominal`; sheet and full resistance sensitivities in @sec-corner-cmos5l-resistance |
: Capacitance components and selection examples {#tbl-corner-availability tbl-colwidths="[25,32,43]"}

Each catalog also declares `capiche-low-c` and `capiche-high-c`, selecting the source-related physical recipes described in @sec-corner-physical-recipes.

The `low` tables agree between the reviewed `hrlc` and `lrlc` styles, and the `high` tables agree between `hrhc` and `lrhc`, for all four PDKs. This permits sharing each capacitance component across those resistance choices; it does not prove that resistance can be factored in the same way.

These are complete tables, not a global scale factor applied to nominal capacitance. A sidewall fit changes its numerator and spacing offset together, so a larger numerator alone does not identify the larger predicted capacitance. Compare the resulting law over the relevant geometry, as described in @sec-parasitic-coefficients.

The component provenance records the source choices that complete the tables:

- `gf180mcuD`: the missing low-C `Metal2`-to-well fringe row uses the same-corner substrate perimeter coefficient, with the established well-plane projection
- `ihp-sg13g2`: the MIM area law varies with the selected data, while its literal edge coefficient remains unchanged, with the separate `cap_cpara` factor excluded from that edge law
- Every PDK retains its explicit diffusion and surrounding-MIM coupling assumptions, without claiming matching physical-stack or device-reference data

{{< pagebreak >}}

#### Holding Resistance Nominal {#sec-corner-sensitivity-catalog}

A sensitivity study can deliberately hold resistance nominal and vary only capacitance. This is a user-defined comparison, not a claim that the foundry specifies that R/C combination as a correlated process corner.

The [complete `sky130A` sensitivity example](../data/tech/sky130A-sensitivity.zip) contains the same component bytes as the bundled catalog, plus two declared scenarios, `nominal-r-low-c` and `nominal-r-high-c`. Unpacking it creates the `sky130A-sensitivity` directory. Its default remains `nominal`, and the custom scenario definitions are recorded in a new catalog-history entry.

The low-C scenario selects:

```json
{
  "id": "nominal-r-low-c",
  "resistance": "nominal",
  "capacitance": "low",
  "process_stack": "nominal",
  "physical_stack_matches": false,
  "device_references": ""
}
```

The high-C scenario selects `"capacitance": "high"` under its distinct scenario identifier. Both use the nominal stack only for compatible layer identities and conductor ordering. The `physical_stack_matches: false` and empty `device_references` declarations prevent that structural use from claiming matched solver geometry or independent corner-specific device references.

{{< pagebreak >}}

#### Comparing Extracted Couplings {#sec-corner-sensitivity-example}

The following commands use the same `sky130A` layout of overlapping `li1` and `met1` plates for all three selections. The `CC` mode retains mutual and substrate capacitances; the nominal resistance selection is present in the catalog but does not add resistors in this mode.

GDS: <https://github.com/iic-jku/klayout-pex/blob/main/testdata/designs/sky130A/test_patterns/overlap_plates_100um_x_100um_li1_m1.gds.gz>

```bash
unzip sky130A-sensitivity.zip
for corner in nominal nominal-r-low-c nominal-r-high-c; do
  kpex extract --pdk sky130A --2.5D --mode CC \
    --tech-catalog sky130A-sensitivity/catalog.pb.json \
    --corner "$corner" \
    --gds overlap_plates_100um_x_100um_li1_m1.gds.gz \
    --out-dir "output/$corner" \
    --out-netlist "output/$corner.spice" \
    --out-result "output/$corner.json"
done
```

{{< include /figures/corner-sensitivity-schematic.qmd >}}

The three extracted couplings in @fig-corner-sensitivity-schematic are:

| Selected scenario | $C_{\mathrm{LU}}$ [fF] | $C_{\mathrm{LS}}$ [fF] | $C_{\mathrm{US}}$ [fF] |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| `nominal-r-low-c` | 203.108 | 305.838 | 162.210 |
| `nominal` | 301.336 | 382.940 | 205.944 |
| `nominal-r-high-c` | 523.375 | 515.064 | 277.637 |
: Extracted capacitances of the same plate layout {#tbl-corner-sensitivity-results tbl-colwidths="[37,21,21,21]"}

$C_{\mathrm{LU}}$ connects `LOWER` ↔ `UPPER`, $C_{\mathrm{LS}}$ connects `LOWER` ↔ `sky130_gnd`, and $C_{\mathrm{US}}$ connects `UPPER` ↔ `sky130_gnd`. These are individual netlist capacitors, not diagonal entries of a capacitance matrix. Each result JSON records the selected component identities and provenance.

The different ratios between the columns show why one multiplier cannot reproduce these tables. To study a distributed RC layout, use `--mode RC` with the same explicitly declared scenarios; resistance then remains nominal while capacitance varies.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Varying GatPoly Sheet Resistance {#sec-corner-gatpoly-sheet}

Both `ihp-sg13g2` and `ihp-sg13cmos5l` provide `gatpoly-low-sheet` and `gatpoly-high-sheet`. They vary only the sheet resistance of extracted `GatPoly` interconnect. Every other layer, contact and via resistance, and all capacitance coefficients, remain explicitly nominal.

The values come directly from each process's maintained interconnect tables: 6.2, 7.0 and 7.8 $\Omega/\square$. The sources and hashes are recorded separately in the [`ihp-sg13g2` low-sheet dataset](../data/tech/ihp-sg13g2/resistance/gatpoly-low-sheet.pb.json) and the [`ihp-sg13cmos5l` low-sheet dataset](../data/tech/ihp-sg13cmos5l/resistance/gatpoly-low-sheet.pb.json).

These are fixed-layout sensitivity selections. They do not apply the thickness or linewidth variation of a full process corner, select a transistor corner, or change temperature. Their nominal stack provides layer identities and ordering; `physical_stack_matches: false` prevents treating it as matched field-solver geometry. These sheet-only scenarios select no device-reference component. An automatic device-capacitance comparison requires a separately justified explicit reference.

#### Comparing Strip Resistance {#sec-corner-gatpoly-example}

The [example LVS database](../data/tech/examples/ihp-gatpoly-strip.lvsdb) contains one 10 µm × 0.5 µm `GatPoly` strip. Ports `A` and `B` span opposite ends, with no contacts and no recognized resistor device. The same conductor and pin definitions apply to both IHP variants.

```bash
for corner in nominal gatpoly-low-sheet gatpoly-high-sheet; do
  kpex extract --pdk ihp-sg13g2 --2.5D --mode R \
    --corner "$corner" --lvsdb ihp-gatpoly-strip.lvsdb \
    --out-dir "output/$corner" \
    --out-netlist "output/$corner.spice"
done
```

For this rectangle, the independent reference is

$$
R_{AB}=R_{\square}\frac{L}{W} = 20R_{\square}.
$$

{{< include /figures/gatpoly-sheet-schematic.qmd >}}

| Selected scenario | Sheet resistance [$\Omega/\square$] | Extracted resistance `A` ↔ `B` [$\Omega$] |
|:---|---:|---:|
| `gatpoly-low-sheet` | 6.2 | 124 |
| `nominal` | 7.0 | 140 |
| `gatpoly-high-sheet` | 7.8 | 156 |
: Terminal resistance of the same fixed strip {#tbl-gatpoly-sheet-results tbl-colwidths="[43,25,32]"}

Repeating the commands with `--pdk ihp-sg13cmos5l` gives the same values. Circuit simulations in `ngspice`, `Xyce` and `VACASK` agree with the sheet law, including strips at the published 0.13 µm interconnect width and the next layout-grid step.

#### Keeping Compact Resistors Separate {#sec-corner-gatpoly-devices}

A recognized `rsil`, `rppd` or `rhigh` resistor keeps its compact model, terminals and dimensions. Its modeled body is excluded from extracted interconnect. The `rsil` model has its own sheet parameters, effective-width correction and contact terms; applying those again to every drawn `GatPoly` polygon would mix two different resistance models.

For this reason, the selectable wire limits are 6.2 and 7.8 $\Omega/\square$ from the interconnect tables, rather than the compact model's 6.02 and 7.98 $\Omega/\square$. No compact-model width shift is applied to the strip. Selecting one of these sensitivities does not select a compact-resistor simulation corner.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Varying CMOS5L Resistance at Fixed Geometry {#sec-corner-cmos5l-resistance}

The `ihp-sg13cmos5l` catalog provides `fixed-layout-low-r` and `fixed-layout-high-r`. They select complete resistance tables for the existing extracted interconnect layers, contacts and vias, while retaining nominal capacitance and the drawn geometry. Select a scenario with the usual extraction options:

```bash
kpex extract --pdk ihp-sg13cmos5l --2.5D --mode RC \
  --corner fixed-layout-low-r --gds design.gds \
  --out-netlist design-low-r.spice --out-result design-low-r.json
```

Use `fixed-layout-high-r` for the corresponding high-resistance extraction, or `nominal` for the unchanged default. The narrower `gatpoly-low-sheet` and `gatpoly-high-sheet` scenarios vary only `GatPoly`; all their other resistance rows remain nominal.

#### Applying Sheet and Contact Laws {#sec-corner-cmos5l-resistance-laws}

A rectangular wire follows $R=R_{\square}L/W$. Each layer has its own sheet resistance; the low/high scenarios therefore do not multiply the entire network by one common factor.

| Conductor | Low | Nominal | High |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| `GatPoly` | 6.2 | 7.0 | 7.8 |
| `Metal1` | 0.085 | 0.110 | 0.135 |
| `Metal2`, `Metal3`, `Metal4` | 0.073 | 0.088 | 0.103 |
| `TopMetal1` | 0.015 | 0.018 | 0.021 |
: `ihp-sg13cmos5l` sheet resistance in $\Omega/\square$ {#tbl-cmos5l-sheet-resistance tbl-colwidths="[40,20,20,20]"}

A contact or via contributes its per-cut resistance. With equipotential terminals on both sides, $N$ identical cuts in parallel give $R=R_{\mathrm{cut}}/N$. A real contact array also has access and spreading resistance in its conductors, which the resistance extraction retains.

| Contact or via | Low | Nominal | High |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Cont` on `nSD` or `pSD` | 8 | 17 | 22 |
| `Cont` on `GatPoly` | 8 | 15 | 20 |
| `Via1`, `Via2`, `Via3` | 5 | 9 | 20 |
| `TopVia1` | 1 | 2.2 | 4 |
: `ihp-sg13cmos5l` contact and via resistance in $\Omega/\mathrm{cut}$ {#tbl-cmos5l-contact-resistance tbl-colwidths="[40,20,20,20]"}

These rows come from the variant's maintained [minimum](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK/blob/e73adb4045731ddec21634146d536380057f6a26/ihp-sg13cmos5l/libs.tech/parasitics/itf/sg13cmos5l_min.itf), [typical](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK/blob/e73adb4045731ddec21634146d536380057f6a26/ihp-sg13cmos5l/libs.tech/parasitics/itf/sg13cmos5l_typ.itf) and [maximum](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK/blob/e73adb4045731ddec21634146d536380057f6a26/ihp-sg13cmos5l/libs.tech/parasitics/itf/sg13cmos5l_max.itf) interconnect tables. In particular, those sources place `TopVia1` between `Metal4` and `TopMetal1` and specify its $0.42\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ square cut directly. This resolves the row left unspecified in the variant's [process-specification contact table](https://github.com/IHP-GmbH/IHP-Open-PDK/blob/e73adb4045731ddec21634146d536380057f6a26/ihp-sg13cmos5l/libs.doc/doc/SG13CMOS5L_os_process_spec.pdf).

#### Interpreting Resistance Sensitivity {#sec-corner-cmos5l-resistance-scope}

The selection changes the interconnect material laws applied to the existing polygons. Compact-device models retain their own internal resistances and geometry rules. Diffusion regions remain ideal device-terminal endpoints under the existing extraction boundary.

The source interconnect files also vary physical parameters, including `GatPoly` thickness. The fixed-layout resistance selections do not apply those geometry changes, temperature variation or compact-model width corrections. They use nominal analytical capacitance and declare no matching field-solver stack or automatic device-capacitance references, as explained in @sec-corner-physical-stack.

The [low-R dataset](../data/tech/ihp-sg13cmos5l/resistance/fixed-layout-low-r.pb.json) and [high-R dataset](../data/tech/ihp-sg13cmos5l/resistance/fixed-layout-high-r.pb.json) record the exact source revisions, hashes and assumptions. Their source-defined resistance bounds are suitable for sensitivity studies; combining them with nonnominal capacitance requires an explicit scenario and a justified interpretation of that combination.

### Varying `sky130A` Resistance {#sec-corner-sky130-resistance}

The `sky130A` catalog provides four fixed-layout resistance sensitivities. Each selects a complete resistance table and the corresponding `low` or `high` capacitance table. `nominal` remains the default.

| Selected scenario | C dataset | MIM sheet resistance [$\Omega/\square$] |
|:---|:---|---:|
| `nominal` | `nominal` | 5.8 |
| [`hrhc-mim-bound`](../data/tech/sky130A/resistance/hrhc-mim-bound.pb.json) | `high` | 6.8 |
| [`hrlc-mim-bound`](../data/tech/sky130A/resistance/hrlc-mim-bound.pb.json) | `low` | 6.8 |
| [`lrhc-mim-bound`](../data/tech/sky130A/resistance/lrhc-mim-bound.pb.json) | `high` | 4.8 |

#### Understanding MIM Bounds {#sec-corner-sky130-mim-bounds}

The [published MIM specification](https://github.com/google/skywater-pdk/blob/7198cf647113f56041e02abf3eb623692820c5e1/docs/rules/device-details/cap_mim/cap_mim-table0.rst) gives `RSCAPM` as 5.8 $\Omega/\square$, bounded by 4.8 and 6.8 $\Omega/\square$, for both MIM top electrodes. These are the `capm` and `capm2` sheet-resistance rows.

The `-mim-bound` selections pair the upper limit with high-R styles and the lower limit with low-R styles. This is an explicit engineering sensitivity policy. The specification does not establish that these limits occur together with the selected R/C model style. The component provenance records that assumption separately from the imported model parameters.

Keep the drawn polygons and contact count fixed when interpreting the result. For a rectangular sheet and $N$ identical contacts in parallel, the material laws are

$$
R_{\mathrm{sheet}}=R_{\square}\frac{L}{W},
\qquad
R_{\mathrm{contacts}}=\frac{R_{\mathrm{cut}}}{N}.
$$

No compact-model linewidth shift is applied to the extracted sheet, and the actual cuts determine $N$. The device models for [`capm`](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/skywater-pdk-libs-sky130_fd_pr/blob/29b55153fd9f4badef05a02667184b81789d1f61/cells/cap_mim_m3/sky130_fd_pr__cap_mim_m3_1.model.spice) and [`capm2`](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/skywater-pdk-libs-sky130_fd_pr/blob/29b55153fd9f4badef05a02667184b81789d1f61/cells/cap_mim_m3/sky130_fd_pr__cap_mim_m3_2.model.spice) have their own effective-width and effective-length corrections and estimated contact counts. Applying those corrections again to the extraction geometry would change the meaning of this fixed-layout comparison.

These selections support analytical extraction with `--2.5D`. They do not specify a combined geometry/material worst case, a transistor corner, temperature, or a probability of the selected values occurring together. Their nominal stack supplies compatible layer identities and ordering; `physical_stack_matches: false` prevents exporting it as matched corner geometry. Automatic corner-specific device-capacitance checks are unavailable unless an independent reference is supplied explicitly.

{{< pagebreak >}}

#### Comparing Via Stacks {#sec-corner-sky130-via-example}

GDS: <https://github.com/iic-jku/klayout-pex/blob/main/testdata/designs/sky130A/test_patterns/r_via_stack_1x1_minsize_poly_to_met5.gds.gz>

### Varying `gf180mcuD` Resistance {#sec-corner-gf180-resistance}

The `gf180mcuD` catalog provides three resistance sensitivities with explicit source assumptions for the existing layout. They retain nominal capacitance and geometry. The default `nominal` scenario remains unchanged.

- `fixed-layout-reference-r` uses a `FuseTop` sheet resistance of $180\,\mathrm{m}\Omega/\square$
- `fixed-layout-high-r` uses the high sheet and contact values, including $207\,\mathrm{m}\Omega/\square$ for `FuseTop`
- `fixed-layout-low-r-ideal-contacts` uses low sheet values, including $153\,\mathrm{m}\Omega/\square$ for `FuseTop`, with an explicitly assumed ideal contact/via connection

The low and high plate values bracket the **$180\,\mathrm{m}\Omega/\square$ reference**, not the default nominal value of **$500\,\mathrm{m}\Omega/\square$**. The scenario names keep that distinction visible when comparing results.

#### Separating Plate Sources {#sec-corner-gf180-plate-sources}

The maintained [interconnect sheet-resistance table](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/gf180mcu-pdk/blob/25ed9c64b64b8e1b93cc4d2d5cade4cd82383a9a/docs/analog/layout/inter_specs/tables_clear/5_Sheet_Rho_table.csv) specifies $0.18\pm0.027\,\Omega/\square$ for the MIM plate.

The named stack is `TiN600AMIMAL2000ATiN350A`. Its $0.295\,\mu\mathrm{m}$ thickness agrees with the [conductor table](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/gf180mcu-pdk/blob/25ed9c64b64b8e1b93cc4d2d5cade4cd82383a9a/docs/analog/layout/inter_specs/tables_clear/3_General_conductor.csv).

The [maintainer's interpretation](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/globalfoundries-pdk-libs-gf180mcu_fd_pr/issues/55#issuecomment-6865435725) supports this material-stack value and assumes that the density options share the plate construction. Applying it to the selected five-metal, 2 fF/µm² `MIM-B` option is an engineering assumption: the option's [electrical table](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/gf180mcu-pdk/blob/25ed9c64b64b8e1b93cc4d2d5cade4cd82383a9a/docs/analog/spice/elec_specs/tables_clear/6_Passive_Elements6.csv) does not specify plate resistance.

`KPEX` retains $500\,\mathrm{m}\Omega/\square$ in `nominal` because that was its established estimate from the 1/1.5 fF specifications. Selecting the new reference is deliberate; installing a newer version does not change the default estimate.

#### Applying Sheet and Contact Values {#sec-corner-gf180-resistance-laws}

The conductor values below use $R=R_{\square}L/W$ at unchanged drawn dimensions. The [electrical sheet-resistance specification](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/gf180mcu-pdk/blob/25ed9c64b64b8e1b93cc4d2d5cade4cd82383a9a/docs/analog/spice/elec_specs/tables_clear/5_General_Specification1.csv) supplies the conductor limits other than the `FuseTop` plate values discussed above. `Metal5` uses the selected thick `11kA` top-metal row, not the ordinary fifth-metal row.

| Conductor | Low | Reference | High |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Poly2` | 1.0 | 7.3 | 15.0 |
| `Metal1`, `Metal2`, `Metal3`, `Metal4` | 0.076 | 0.090 | 0.104 |
| `Metal5` | 0.031 | 0.040 | 0.049 |
| `Nwell` | 800 | 1000 | 1200 |
| `FuseTop` | 0.153 | 0.180 | 0.207 |
: Fixed-layout `gf180mcuD` sheet sensitivity in $\Omega/\square$ {#tbl-gf180-sheet-sensitivity tbl-colwidths="[40,20,20,20]"}

::: {.content-visible when-format="pdf"}

{{< pagebreak >}}

:::

Each cut contributes its per-cut resistance. With equipotential landing pads, $N$ identical cuts in parallel give $R=R_{\mathrm{cut}}/N$. The extraction also retains conductor access and spreading resistance for real layouts.

| Contact or via | Ideal-contact assumption | Reference | High |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| `Contact` on `Nplus` or `Nwell` | 0 | 6.3 | 15 |
| `Contact` on `Pplus` | 0 | 5.2 | 15 |
| `Contact` on `Poly2` | 0 | 5.9 | 15 |
| `Via1`, `Via2`, `Via3`, `Via4` | 0 | 4.5 | 15 |
: Fixed-layout `gf180mcuD` contact sensitivity in $\Omega/\mathrm{cut}$ {#tbl-gf180-contact-sensitivity tbl-colwidths="[40,20,20,20]"}

The primary [contact specification](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/gf180mcu-pdk/blob/25ed9c64b64b8e1b93cc4d2d5cade4cd82383a9a/docs/analog/spice/elec_specs/tables_clear/5_General_Specification2.csv) writes `--` for all minimum values. That means **unspecified**, not zero. The separately named ideal-contact scenario follows the explicit zeros in the maintained [`MAGIC` low-R extraction block](https://github.com/fossi-foundation/open-pdks/blob/5740c4a81c42f9fe4af5ef2ee258a99151053d28/gf180mcu/magic/gf180mcu-extract.tech#L330-L435). It is not a measured physical lower limit. The reference and high datasets record only the primary nonzero values.

The `Poly2` reference contact remains 5.9 Ω/cut. The contact from `Nwell` uses the established `Nplus` contact mapping, and the MIM top landing uses the `Via4` per-cut law. With `--blackbox y`, recognized compact devices retain their own models and terminal boundaries (@sec-first-steps-run-2_5d).

#### Selecting the Sensitivity {#sec-corner-gf180-resistance-selection}

```bash
kpex extract --pdk gf180mcuD --2.5D --mode RC --blackbox y \
  --corner fixed-layout-reference-r --gds design.gds \
  --out-netlist design-reference-r.spice
```

Select `fixed-layout-high-r` or `fixed-layout-low-r-ideal-contacts` explicitly for the other comparisons. Do not interpret the default `nominal` result as the midpoint of this plate-resistance range.

The [ideal-contact low-R dataset](../data/tech/gf180mcuD/resistance/fixed-layout-low-r-ideal-contacts.pb.json), [reference dataset](../data/tech/gf180mcuD/resistance/fixed-layout-reference-r.pb.json), and [high-R dataset](../data/tech/gf180mcuD/resistance/fixed-layout-high-r.pb.json) record the exact source revisions, hashes and assumptions.

#### Limits {#sec-corner-gf180-resistance-limits}

These are fixed-layout sensitivities. They do not establish a foundry-qualified 2 fF plate law, correlated R/C corners, simultaneous manufacturing extrema, width or temperature corrections, or statistical coverage. They select no automatic device-capacitance reference and declare no matching field-solver stack. Combining them with nonnominal capacitance needs a separately declared scenario and a justified interpretation.

An ideal contact merges its electrical nodes. Separately named SPICE ports on the same node retain the existing 1 mΩ label tie. That export tie is not a physical contact value and does not divide by the number of cuts.


### Matching Physical Geometry to Analytical Tables {#sec-corner-physical-stack}

Analytical extraction needs conductor ordering and connectivity from the stack, while its numerical capacitance comes from tables. A table-only corner can therefore use a nominal stack explicitly for structural purposes.

A field solver instead calculates capacitance from physical geometry and materials. Exporting nominal geometry under a nonnominal label would not reproduce a table corner. A scenario consequently declares whether its selected physical stack matches the scenario.

| Requested operation | Required evidence |
|:---|:---|
| `--2.5D` extraction | Complete R/C datasets and compatible conductor identities |
| `kpex pex25d` | A declared matching physical stack |
| `--fastcap` or `--fastercap` | A declared matching physical stack |
| Automatic `--check-device-caps` | A device-reference dataset for the scenario |
: Capabilities checked before layout loading {#tbl-corner-capabilities tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

A missing capability produces a diagnostic before extraction. Device checks can instead use an explicitly supplied reference JSON file. Its physical assumptions remain the user's choice. A nominal reference is never inherited automatically by a scenario that declares none.

The matching-stack declaration records a dataset contract, not foundry certification. It is checked before layout loading; availability of individual physical profiles is checked against the extracted shapes afterward. A numerical recipe may vary permittivity, thickness or manufactured width. Those choices require their own sources and must not be inferred from the spelling of a corner name.

{{< pagebreak >}}

{{< include /doc/_sec_physical_corner_recipes.qmd >}}

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Selecting Device-Capacitance References {#sec-corner-device-references}

A capacitance component describes the extracted interconnect. A device-reference component supplies independent model expressions for `--check-device-caps` (@sec-device-capacitance-check). Selecting one does not select the other. The catalog must name the intended reference explicitly.

The additional reference components cover these MIM models:

| Technology | Supported device | Reference component IDs |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `sky130A` | Both mapped MIM plate options | `hrhc`, `hrlc`, `lrhc`, `lrlc` |
| `gf180mcuD` | `cap_mim_2f0fF` | `low`, `high` |
| `ihp-sg13g2` | `cap_cmim` | `low`, `high` |
| `ihp-sg13cmos5l` | No additional MIM reference component | No additional component |
: Explicit source-backed MIM reference components {#tbl-corner-device-reference-coverage tbl-colwidths="[25,43,32]"}

For `sky130A`, the two mapped devices are:

- `sky130_fd_pr__model__cap_mim`
- `sky130_fd_pr__model__cap_mim_m4`

The references describe low-frequency mutual capacitance at zero bias and zero mismatch. The model reference temperatures are 27 °C for `sky130A` and `ihp-sg13g2`, and 25 °C for `gf180mcuD`. Series resistance, leakage and substrate shunts are separate observables.

The source equations are checked against pinned compact-model simulations. For a two-terminal device, the mutual capacitance follows the off-diagonal admittance:

$$
C_{AB}=-\frac{\operatorname{Im}Y_{AB}}{\omega}.
$$

The comparison uses frequencies low enough that series resistance does not materially change this observable. It does not interpret leakage conductance as capacitance or compare the sum of all capacitances attached to a net.

#### Preserving the Model's Corner Law {#sec-corner-device-model-law}

Different models vary different terms:

- `sky130A`: the R/C style changes the effective dimensions as well as area and edge coefficients. Two styles with the same C suffix can therefore require different reference expressions
- `gf180mcuD`: the supported 2 fF MIM option scales both area and perimeter terms by its own MIM corner parameter
- `ihp-sg13g2`: `cap_cmim` varies its area density while retaining the literal edge density of $40\,\mathrm{aF}/\mu\mathrm m$. Its multiplier applies once to the complete device capacitance

For the IHP reference, with mapped dimensions expressed in micrometres,

$$
C_{\mathrm{reference}}=m\left[C_AWL+2C_P(W+L)\right].
$$

The `low` and `high` components use $C_A=1.35$ and $1.65\,\mathrm{fF}/\mu\mathrm m^2$, respectively, while $C_P=0.04\,\mathrm{fF}/\mu\mathrm m$ stays fixed. A global multiplier applied to nominal capacitance would incorrectly change that edge term too.

{{< pagebreak >}}

#### Comparing MIM Plates at Two Capacitance Selections {#sec-corner-device-reference-example}

The [complete MIM comparison catalog](../data/tech/ihp-mim-reference.zip) declares `mim-low-c` and `mim-high-c`. They pair the corresponding C tables and device-reference component while holding resistance nominal. This is an explicitly authored sensitivity comparison, without a claim of correlated resistance or matching field-solver geometry.

The low selection contains:

```json
{
  "id": "mim-low-c",
  "resistance": "nominal",
  "capacitance": "low",
  "process_stack": "nominal",
  "device_references": "low",
  "physical_stack_matches": false
}
```

The high selection names `high` for both capacitance and device references. Neither selection inherits the nominal MOM references.

GDS: <https://github.com/iic-jku/klayout-pex/blob/main/testdata/designs/ihp-sg13g2/test_patterns/cap_cmim_20um_x_20um_over_m4_wire.gds.gz>

The layout contains a 20 µm × 20 µm `cap_cmim` with terminals `A` ↔ `B`, above a separate `Metal4` route. Set `KPEX_DIR` to the source checkout, then run:

```bash
unzip ihp-mim-reference.zip
pattern=cap_cmim_20um_x_20um_over_m4_wire
layouts="$KPEX_DIR/testdata/designs/ihp-sg13g2/test_patterns"
lvsdbs="$KPEX_DIR/testdata/lvsdb/ihp-sg13g2/test_patterns"
for corner in mim-low-c mim-high-c; do
  kpex extract --pdk ihp-sg13g2 --2.5D --mode CC \
    --blackbox y --halo 8 --scale y \
    --gds "$layouts/$pattern.gds.gz" \
    --lvsdb "$lvsdbs/$pattern.lvsdb.gz" \
    --tech-catalog ihp-mim-reference/catalog.pb.json \
    --corner "$corner" --check-device-caps \
    --out-dir "output/$corner" \
    --out-result "output/$corner.json"
done
```

| Selected scenario | Marker coupling [fF] | Model reference [fF] | Ratio |
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
| `mim-low-c` | 540.0 | 543.2 | 0.994109 |
| `mim-high-c` | 660.0 | 663.2 | 0.995175 |
: Recorded device-local comparisons of the same MIM layout {#tbl-corner-device-reference-results tbl-colwidths="[31,25,25,19]"}

{{< include /figures/device-corner-reference-schematic.qmd >}}

In this LVS definition, both device-owned plates stop at the MIM rectangle. The lower electrode's 2 µm overhang is ordinary `Metal5`, outside that ownership region. The marker observer therefore excludes fringe coupling to the overhang and reports area coupling only, while the model includes its 3.2 fF perimeter contribution.

The separate route's coupling is also outside this device-local comparison. Both results are `informational`: no acceptance bound was supplied. Their ratios compare different observation domains and must not be interpreted as qualification of the complete device capacitance.

#### Limits of Device-Corner References {#sec-corner-device-reference-limits}

The components cover only the listed MIM models. MOM devices, RF MIM models, other MIM density options and unlisted capacitor types remain unchecked. A layout with no supported references fails a requested automatic check with an explanation.

The existing `nominal` reference component is unchanged. In particular, the IHP nominal MOM engineering estimates remain available under their original assumptions; the new MIM components do not supply nonnominal MOM laws or automatically add nominal MIM checks.

The selected expressions reject nonpositive effective dimensions and invalid multiplicities. They do not replace PDK layout rules, qualify arbitrary bias or temperature, or define statistical correlations with transistor corners. A custom explicit reference file remains available when another independently justified comparison is needed.

{{< pagebreak >}}

### Recording What Was Used {#sec-corner-provenance}

`kpex_result.json`, or the path selected by `--out-result`, records `technology_selection`:

- Technology and scenario identifiers
- Catalog path and SHA256 of its exact bytes
- Catalog description, structured provenance and data revision
- Selected component identifiers, content hashes, source records, assumptions and revision histories
- Hash of the complete selected input technology
- Whether a matching physical stack and device references were declared

Sources, source references and revision history are validated before using the selected data. A missing source identity, unknown source identifier, invalid calendar date or inconsistent current revision is an error.

Each component file is checked against the catalog's byte hash. Changing or reformatting a file while retaining an old byte hash is detected. A byte-identical copy retains the same hash. The resolved content identities are separate: irrelevant JSON object-key order does not change the identity, while physically significant stack and terminal order is retained.

`technology_selection.resolved_technology_sha256` identifies the selected input before runtime overrides. An extraction with `--halo 3` records its effective halo separately as `halo_um`, and preserves the override in `arguments`. Keep the complete result with the netlist rather than using a scenario label alone as a reproducibility key.

`PEX25D` metadata records the selected `process_corner`. Physical-stack identity remains distinct from the capacitance-table identity, which matters when comparing geometry generation with fitted or imported coefficients.

### Limits {#sec-corner-limits}

- Explicit `--corner` or `--tech-catalog` cannot be combined with `--magic`, whose installed technology and extraction style are selected independently
- A different conductor topology or layout/LVS interface needs a separate technology catalog
- No voltage, temperature, statistical variation or transistor-model selection is inferred
- An analytical corner without a matching physical recipe cannot be exported as corner-matched solver geometry
- Only the scenarios declared by the supplied catalog can be selected
